target_customer: Restaurants, dark kitchens and food shops in Latin America that want to sell directly to their own customers
problem: Delivery marketplaces charge restaurants commissions of 30 percent or more and keep the customer relationship; Justo gives them their own online store and delivery at lower cost.
business_model: Commission on orders (stated as 7 to 15 percent) plus software, logistics, marketing and lending services
product_category: Restaurant e-commerce, ordering and last mile delivery platform

founders.name: Rodrigo Segal
founders.background_notes: Co-founder and CEO per YC page and Chilean press. Background not found.

founders.name: Nicolás López Jullian
founders.background_notes: Founder and CPO per YC page; LatamList calls him founder and CEO. Background not found.

competitors.name: Didi Food
competitors.what: Food delivery marketplace app in Mexico

competitors.name: Uber Eats
competitors.what: Delivery marketplace with commission set per restaurant

technical_complexity.rationale: White label stores, courier dispatch and payments across several countries are standard engineering, with operational complexity in logistics.

defensibility.rationale: Restaurants that run their store and delivery through Justo face some switching cost, but low commissions can be matched and couriers multi-home.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Marketplaces kept their commission model; sources found do not show them copying a white label store product.

market_need_then: COVID-19 closed dining rooms in 2020 and restaurants complained about 30 to 40 percent marketplace commissions, which drove them to Justo per Contxto and El CEO coverage.

branding.name_origin: YC page says the name means fair in Spanish, reflecting the aim of offering restaurants technology at a fairer price.
branding.domain_note: Uses getjusto.com with a get prefix; history not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Positions itself as the partner behind the restaurant's store, not a marketplace

branding.brand_signature: Low commission, about one third of marketplaces

brand_strength.rationale: Meaningful Spanish name tied to the fair pricing message and regional press coverage, but it is confusable with the unrelated Mexican grocer Justo (Jusuto).

outcome_analysis: Justo rode the 2020 pandemic delivery surge into six countries and 190 staff on a small 2.3 million round, then cut 45 to 80 people in 2022 as investors warned of a harder economy and a further raise was dropped. The founders said they expected breakeven. It remains active with a broader product suite including POS and lending.
notes: Two unrelated companies share the name: this Chilean restaurant platform and Jüsto, a Mexican online grocer (rounds of 12M, 65M, 152M and a shutdown in Mexico and Brazil belong to the grocer and are excluded). The 2.3M round is stated by LatamList and Diario Financiero; the stage label is not given. Founding year differs between sources (2018 and 2019).
